claims.text: Existing uncertainty quantification methods for LLM responses often overlook the complex nature of LLMs and the uniqueness of in-context learning.
Predictive uncertainty in in-context learning stems in part from the provided demonstrations, which corresponds to aleatoric uncertainty.
Predictive uncertainty in in-context learning stems in part from ambiguities tied to model configurations, which corresponds to epistemic uncertainty.
The proposed uncertainty estimation method operates in an unsupervised, plug-and-play fashion for in-context learning predictions.
Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of decomposing uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components in in-context learning.

evidence.description: Existing works have been devoted to quantifying the uncertainty in LLM's response, but they often overlook the complex nature of LLMs and the uniqueness of in-context learning.
such uncertainties may stem from both the provided demonstrations (aleatoric uncertainty)
and ambiguities tied to the model's configurations (epistemic uncertainty).
The proposed method offers an unsupervised way to understand the prediction of in-context learning in a plug-and-play fashion.
Extensive experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the decomposition.

methodologies.name: Uncertainty Decomposition for In-Context Learning (UQ_ICL)
methodologies.description: An unsupervised, plug-and-play method that quantifies and decomposes predictive uncertainty into demonstration-level aleatoric uncertainty and model-configuration epistemic uncertainty.

limitations.text: Existing works quantifying uncertainty in LLM responses often overlook the complex nature of LLMs and the uniqueness of in-context learning.
